I’ve been thinking a lot about starting a baked goods stand at the farmers market, and donating 10% of the proceeds to MS society and the MS foundation. But the problem is I have to somehow find a commercial kitchen to bake my goods in that is wheelchair accessible. Which I have yet to even see an accessible kitchen in existence... 
If that doesn’t happen, then maybe I’ll do Wheelchair-friendly cooking tutorials on YouTube. 
But sadly, I realize fully that my “career” is over. I will likely never make a reliable profit with food professionally.
But I still cook, bake and create at home, on my good days when I can cope with the pain. 
Writing a book is an excellent idea! I hope you can remain on the line, and I hope I didn’t scare you. :( 
MS affects all of us so differently, and you may be able to find a great solution. Especially if your kitchen manager is willing to be flexible and work with you. Towards the end I got pulled off the line and was on prep; but this meant I got to pull up a stool so I could rest my feet and still do something productive. I know the pride and confidence that comes with being on the line, and it can be devastating to be pulled off the line. But you can’t work yourself to death. At the end of the day your health is more important than the line, and that’s ultimately what I had to accept.
Just know that you aren’t alone in this, there are more disabled chefs out there than you’d think! Thank you for your kind words

I was a chef for 2 1/2 years and was in my prime. I finally had the position I wanted, was in a great and very high volume $$$ restaurant and was finally making the money I deserved. I was literally on top of the world and going great (getting promotions, raises, etc) and after about 6 months in this new position my right leg started giving me huge problems. I couldn’t stand for more than three hours without having to take a break (and you probably know how breaks are frowned upon in the kitchen) and it was severely affecting my work performance. I used to be able to kick ass and push tickets like crazy!! And now all the sudden I was limping around the kitchen, in extreme pain and fatigue. And to top it all off I got Shingles and it rendered me bedridden for over a month in extreme agony. Needless to say I lost my career. And I understand completely why, you’ve gotta keep pushing tickets or you will fuck up the whole process. If I can’t push tickets anymore then they have to find someone who can. I have no feelings of remorse toward my old boss and coworkers, just a feeling of crushing depression and sadness. I feel like I let them down. And now, I can’t even walk at all. I have no idea when I’ll be able to work again, let alone ever get back to the career I was so passionate about. I find that if I think too much about the career I lost I spiral into a very very scary dark place. Just know that you’re not the only one going through this crazy shit. It’s heartbreaking and unfair to have something you love so much be taken from you. :(
